- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per period to avoid overcorrection.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often underestimates upside — increase forecast baseline by 1–2% to account for policy-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse the trend by reducing forecast slope or adding a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per period.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- When multiple auction events occur in 3–5 days, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% per event to avoid volatility overfitting.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction, not just price history.
